title: Audit derivatives and compile a tiny transformation

stages.title: Directional products and exact curvature
stages.evidence: Three independent Jacobian/Hessian comparisons, adjoint identity and shape contract
stages.expected: PASS stage 1: three independent Jacobian/Hessian references, adjoint identity and shape rejection
stages.diagnosis: If the HVP disagrees with J-transpose-J times the direction, include the residual-weighted second derivative term.

stages.title: Exact custom derivative contracts
stages.evidence: Stable extreme values, analytic slopes/Hessians, cotangent linearity and transformation-boundary evidence
stages.expected: PASS stage 2: stable exact custom primals, gradients, curvature, cotangent linearity, common shifts and custom-VJP boundary
stages.diagnosis: If first derivatives pass but second derivatives fail, inspect detached derivative coefficients or saved residuals.

stages.title: A compiled primitive-level transformation
stages.evidence: Explicit rules, random-shape expression oracles, captured constants, multiple inputs/outputs and unsupported-operation rejection
stages.expected: PASS stage 3: random shapes, independent expression oracles, constants, multiple inputs/outputs, compiled changed values and explicit unsupported/signature rejection
stages.diagnosis: If the primal is correct but the tangent is not, audit multiplication and constant tangents before changing compiler settings.

rubric: Explain input directions and output cotangents using independent Jacobians
Verify an exact Hessian-vector product rather than substituting Gauss–Newton
Defend exact custom JVP/VJP rules, stability, seed linearity and higher derivatives
Implement explicit primitive tangent rules with captured and literal constants
Reject unsupported primitives and shape/dtype violations
Verify interpreted and compiled transformed outputs on changed values and shapes
Explain limits of the supported subset and distinguish IR inspection from performance measurement
setupNote: Extract the ZIP, install requirements-cpu.txt in your course environment, and run commands from the extracted top folder. The scaffold enables CPU float64 examples; no compiler or accelerator installation is required.
